notes:
STRONG SINGLE PROMPT arm, rung n09 (9 named referents in the ledger: Marlpit ward, Ferry Bank estate, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Barrowfield Youth Justice Team, the Second Chances course of Jan-Apr 2025, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Wharfside Boathouse, Priya Raval the delivery coordinator, and Northgate Minibus Hire). ONE call, finish_reason=stop, native_finish_reason=end_turn, no retry, no repair, no edit. Output written to out-n09-D.md exactly as returned; the only removal was the tool's own trailing metadata line naming the model and generation id, which is transport annotation and not model output.

PROMPT: the n03/n06 arm-D prompt held fixed, so this rung differs from n06-D only by the ledger it carries. It is a single 3,025-word user message (no system prompt) with the full verbatim funder guidance, the published criteria and weights, the organisation record, all 17 non-meta ledger items with source tags, an absolute grounding block (explicit do-not-invent list covering staff/venue/street/partner/vendor names, registration numbers, statistics, past dates and prior results), an explicit statement that a thin answer that is true beats a rich answer that is fabricated, permission to design the FUTURE freely, an internal-consistency block demanding the budget arithmetic close and one cohort structure carry through Q3/Q4/budget, a criteria-targeting block, an anti-LLM-register style brief, the verbatim required headings, and the 1,200-word hard limit with a 1,150-1,190 target. Five edits carry the prompt from n06 to n09, all factual rather than structural: the fixture disclaimer names the three extra fixture referents (Ferry Bank, Barrowfield Youth Justice Team, Wharfside Boathouse); 'fourteen items' becomes 'seventeen items' in two places; E-WEB-7/8/9 are appended to the ledger listing; and the named-place, progression and capability hints are corrected to describe what this ledger actually supplies (a second named neighbourhood, a second named venue with its hire rate, a second named partner organisation). One sentence was added to the progression hint noting that the 31 first-term attenders at Ferry Bank is an attendance count, which the fund explicitly says is not an outcome - this is a restatement of the funder's own published rule applied to a new ledger item, not a new hint class. No other hint was added that n06-D did not have an equivalent of. The prompt file is at n09D/prompt.txt. No analyze stage, no org research, no voice stage, no strategy reservation, no design object, no validation loop, no claim ledger.

CALL PARAMETERS: max_tokens 12000, reasoning_effort low, no provider pin - identical to n03-D and n06-D. Native usage 6,430 prompt / 4,135 completion, of which 797 were reasoning tokens. Cost is OpenRouter's own billed figure (total_cost 0.135525) read back from get-generation, not an estimate from token counts. Provider: Claude Platform on AWS, permaslug anthropic/claude-opus-5-20260723, generation time 53.6s.

WORD COUNTS - counted with wc -w and a python section splitter, not by any model. word_count 1690 is the whole file including headings, budget table and declaration, the same basis used for the other arms at this rung.

*** HARD WORD LIMIT BREACHED. *** The funder-relevant count is the five answers Q1-Q5 excluding heading lines: 1,365 words. The stated hard limit is 1,200. This application is 165 words over, 13.75 per cent over, and under the fund's own rule ('applications over it are returned unread and cannot be resubmitted in the same round') it would not be assessed at all. Per-section body counts: Q1 289, Q2 319, Q3 320, Q4 255, Q5 182; budget table 199 and declaration 77 are excluded by the funder's rule. This is not a rounding question and it is not a repairable defect within the terms of this arm: the arm is one call, take what comes back, and what came back is over the limit. The prompt stated the limit twice, gave a 1,150-1,190 target, and told the model that going over means the application is returned unread. The same prompt produced 1,186 words at n03 (28 under) and 1,186 at n06 (14 under). Only the ledger changed. The most economical reading of the three rungs is that as the ledger gets richer this single call spends the extra material rather than trading it against the existing material, and the limit is what gives way. That is the measurement.

ARITHMETIC VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (python, not by a model). Budget closes: the eight direct lines sum to 46,440 exactly as stated; 12 per cent of 46,440 is 5,572.80 and the single overhead line states 5,560, so it is under the cap and the stated 11.97 per cent is correct; 46,440 + 5,560 = 52,000 which matches the stated total request and sits inside the GBP 25,000-75,000 band. Unit costs reconcile to the ledger prices where stated: Marlpit venue (48 + 30) x GBP 40 = 3,120, Ferry Bank venue 20 x GBP 120 = 2,400, transport 24 x GBP 95 = 2,280, participants 64 x GBP 60 = 3,840, sessional 700 x GBP 14 = 9,800. Cohort structure carries cleanly: 4 x 16 = 64 through Q3, Q4 and the budget; 6 trips x 4 cohorts = 24. College referral maths is exact: the 18-of-27 record (66.7 per cent) applied to 24 referrals gives 16, as stated. The 18-month period 1 March 2027 to 31 August 2028 is at the ceiling and starts after the 12 February 2027 decision date.

ARITHMETIC DEFECT FOUND (reported, not fixed - the output is what the single call returned). The Ferry Bank venue line is under-costed. Q3 sets cohorts 1 and 3 at 'two evenings a week for twelve weeks' in Marlpit and describes cohorts 2 and 4 as the same course run at Wharfside Boathouse, which is 2 cohorts x 12 weeks x 2 evenings = 48 sessions. The budget funds 20 days at GBP 120 = GBP 2,400. Forty-eight days at the ledger's own GBP 120 rate is GBP 5,760, so the line is short by GBP 3,360, about 7 per cent of direct costs. The Marlpit line by contrast is costed correctly at the full 48 course evenings plus 30 follow-through evenings. Note the internal asymmetry: the document costs the Marlpit half of the same course at 48 evenings and the Ferry Bank half at 20 days. This is the same failure class the worker's deterministic consistency checker cannot catch: it never sums anything and its comparison is one-directional (n > target * 1.01), so an understatement passes by construction.

SECOND ARITHMETIC DEFECT. Q5 costs the continuing annual cohort at 'about GBP 3,400: 24 evenings of hall or boathouse hire, three minibus trips and participant costs'. Neither reading reconciles. All-hall: 24 x 40 + 3 x 95 + 16 x 60 = GBP 2,205. All-boathouse: 24 x 120 + 3 x 95 + 16 x 60 = GBP 4,125. The stated figure sits between the two and is derivable from neither. Also, Q3 states the follow-through drop-in as 'fortnightly ... 30 evenings across the grant' while Q5 prices the same drop-in at 26 evenings a year; fortnightly over an 18-month grant is 39 evenings, not 30, so the in-grant count and the continuation rate disagree.

TARGET-SETTING DEFECT. Q4 asserts 'We are holding the completion rate and the progression rate flat'. The completion claim is true: 19/24 is 79.17 per cent and 51/64 is 79.7 per cent. The progression claim is false on either reading. The Second Chances base rate is 11 of 24 starters (45.83 per cent) or 11 of 19 finishers (57.89 per cent); the plan states 32 of 64 starters (50.0 per cent) or 32 of 51 finishers (62.75 per cent). Both are above the base rate the document cites as its authority, so the sentence claiming flatness is contradicted by the numbers in the same paragraph. This is the identical defect observed at n06-D, where the same prompt produced a progression target above its own cited base rate while calling it conservative.

FAILURE THRESHOLD IS SOFT. Q4 answers the funder's 'what would count as this not having worked' question with a specific number, which is what the criterion asks for, but the number is fewer than 20 of 64 reaching a next step - 31.25 per cent, well below the 45.83 per cent the organisation has already achieved once. The bar it sets is easy to clear. Same as n06-D.

GROUNDING AUDIT (manual, against the 17 ledger items): no invented fact about the applicant was found. All nine named referents were used and used in load-bearing positions rather than decoratively - Marlpit and Ferry Bank each carry their own cohorts and their own budget venue line, St Aidan's Parish Hall and Wharfside Boathouse both at their ledger hire rates, Dunmore Sixth Form College as the named progression destination with its ledger conversion rate driving the target, Barrowfield Youth Justice Team as a named recruitment route with its ledger referral count, Northgate Minibus Hire at its ledger per-trip price, Priya Raval carrying the capability claim and named as the owner of both the curriculum and the measurement spreadsheet, and the Second Chances 24/19/11 record as the stated basis for the targets. Every past-tense claim traces to a ledger item: 2016 constitution, 41,000 population, six staff / 4.2 FTE, 25 volunteers, GBP 214,000 expenditure, two years of accounts, the three service lines, three evenings a week in Marlpit, the 38 per cent lowest-decile figure at the 2021 census, the October 2024 Ferry Bank opening and its 31 first-term attenders, the nine youth justice referrals of which six live in Ferry Bank, the 27/18 college record, the 46 supper-club sittings, the 14 minibus trips and the 18 boathouse days across two summers. Derived figures are correct arithmetic on ledger items (24 - 19 = 5 'never finished', 19 - 11 = 8 'finished without reaching a next step', 27 - 18 = 9 'did not enrol'). No charity number was written or placeholdered. No staff, trustee, participant, street, employer or additional vendor name was invented; unnamed future partners appear by function ('a further education provider', 'local employers'); the declaration signs with role titles only. Zero bracketed placeholders. Zero em dashes. None of the prompt's banned consultancy register appears. The 31 first-term attenders are explicitly handled as reach and not as an outcome, as the fund requires.

GROUNDING SLIPS (two, both unlicensed substitutions rather than fabrications). (1) Q5 says the trustees can carry the continuation cost 'within a GBP 214,000 turnover'; the ledger states GBP 214,000 of expenditure, not turnover or income. The two are not the same number. This is the identical slip n06-D made with the identical prompt, so it is reproducible rather than incidental, and it matters here because the fund's eligibility test is an income ceiling. (2) Q2 says 'we run six weekly sessions in them', attributing the six weekly sessions across both Marlpit and Ferry Bank; E-WEB-5 places all six in Marlpit. Ferry Bank session frequency is not in the ledger at all.

OTHER HONEST WEAKNESSES OBSERVED. (3) Eligibility against the GBP 1.5m income ceiling is left inferable from the expenditure figure rather than stated, again as at n06-D. (4) The 18-month period runs to the funder's ceiling exactly, with cohort 4 and its six-month follow-through partly outside the funded window; the document does not address who pays for the tail, the same structural gap seen at n06-D. (5) 'Registration with the charity regulator is current' is licensed by E-INTAKE-2's instruction to treat registration as confirmed, but it is stated as a positive fact rather than flagged as a self-certification. (6) The independent evaluator is a real budget line (GBP 2,500) for a fund that says it does not fund research; it is framed as evaluation, which is an eligible category, so this is defensible but it is the one line an assessor might query.
